The interfaces between hardware and motion

A motor command is only useful when the hardware, feedback, units, and communication agree.

I co-developed a controller schematic based on an open-source architecture, collaborated on layout, and worked through manufacturing, hand assembly, rework, and bench testing. Alongside the board development, I built Python and C++ communication tools for the robot’s motor drivers.

Electronics and prototype evidence

Building on Berkeley Humanoid Lite and Recoil, I worked on schematic adaptation and packaging, collaborated on PCB layout, and developed the host-side integration.

Communication and control

The host tools handle SocketCAN communication, telemetry, fault logging, and motor coordinate conventions. I worked with watchdogs, bounded commands, readbacks, and isolated tests to investigate wiring, adapters, firmware timing, and behavior under load.

Position, velocity, and feedforward torque
τ = Kp(qdes − q) + Kd(q̇des − q̇) + τff

The custom Recoil control mode combines position error, velocity error, and a feedforward torque command. The documented interface uses output-joint radians, radians per second, and newton-metres; this implementation uses its own packet format.

What worked, and what needs another revision

PROJECT STATUS

The first custom board did not reach working operation.

The board was fabricated, assembled, reworked, and tested, but the first custom FOC PCB did not operate successfully. I used off-the-shelf drivers to keep the robot integration work moving. The failure made power, sensing, wiring, and firmware bring-up checks more concrete and informed the next controller revision.

I treat the custom board, the firmware extension, and the robot’s motor-driver integration as separate engineering outcomes. Each needs its own evidence.
